# Test data

Every file here must come from a permissively licensed source or be generated by a reference tool acting
as an oracle. Record the source, its license and its version or commit next to each file (in this README).
Vendored files are fetched by [`scripts/vendor-testdata.sh`](../scripts/vendor-testdata.sh) at the pinned
commits below; do not edit them by hand.

**Never add GPL-licensed vectors**, such as dpkg's `t-version.c`, rpm's `tests/rpmvercmp.at`, apk-tools'
`test/unit/version.data`, or univers' `alpine_test.txt` and `rpmvercmp.at`, **or files derived from them**
(see [Excluded](#excluded)). See also [docs/RESEARCH.md](../docs/RESEARCH.md#licensing-of-test-data).

([vers-spec#146](https://github.com/package-url/vers-spec/pull/146)).

Where polyver deliberately gives a different result than a vendored case expects, the case is listed
with the reason in [`test/support/divergences.ts`](../test/support/divergences.ts). It still runs and
asserts polyver's result.

## Oracle vectors

`pnpm oracle <deb|rpm|apk|maven>` regenerates `oracle/<eco>.txt` and `oracle/<eco>-validity.txt` from committed
inputs only, so a rerun is byte-identical. Its inputs are:

- hand-written edge cases in `scripts/oracle/cases/<eco>.txt`, written from the format documentation
  (Debian Policy §5.6.12, Fedora's versioning guidelines and its examples, the apk version format, the
  POM version order specification and its examples), not from any test suite;
- the index sample, refreshed with `pnpm oracle:harvest <eco>`;
- grammar-based random versions and single-edit mutations from a fixed-seed PRNG
  (`scripts/oracle/generate.ts`).

Each version is first checked for validity (`dpkg --validate-version`, `apk version -c`, `rpm.ver`,
`new ComparableVersion`), and only pairs of valid versions are compared, because dpkg merely warns about
some invalid versions and apk prints nothing for them.

The generated pairs were checked against the GPL suites (dpkg's `t-version.c` and
`scripts/t/Dpkg_Version.t`, rpm's `rpmvercmp.at`, apk-tools' `version.data`) on 2026-10-26. Only a few
trivial pairs occur there too: `1.0`/`1.1` and `8`/`9` for apk, and pairs of `0`, `00`, `1` and `1:0`
for deb. None occur for rpm. This is the same bar as the osv-scalibr generated files.

**apk-tools 2.x.** polyver follows apk-tools 3 (Alpine 3.23 and later). On the same inputs, apk-tools
2.14.12 (`alpine:3.22`) differs in two ways:

- validity: 2.x rejects a `~hash` and accepts some malformed versions, such as `1.0-r` and `a1`;
- order: 109 of 3,168 pairs differ, all involving a `~hash` or a non-first component with a leading
  zero. The latter occurs in real versions (59 of 932 sampled, mostly Perl modules); for example, 3.x
  orders `0.002-r6 > 0.0.202605-r0` and 2.x the opposite.

**Maven 3.9.** polyver follows maven-artifact 4.0.0-rc-7. `pnpm oracle maven` also runs 3.9.16 and
writes `oracle/maven-3.9.txt`, which no test reads. It orders 110 of the 7,883 pairs differently, none of
them between two versions from the Maven Central sample; for example, 4.0 orders `1.0-1 > 1-1` and
`10.0.0.beta0 > 10.0.0.beta`, where 3.9 finds both pairs equal. See
[docs/RESEARCH.md](../docs/RESEARCH.md#findings-from-the-maven-oracle-2026-10-28).

## Excluded

These files are published under a permissive license but are copied from GPL test suites, so they are
not vendored. Checked on 2026-10-26.

| File | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| vers-spec `tests/alpine_version_cmp_test.json` | All 716 version pairs appear verbatim in apk-tools' `test/version.data` (GPL-2.0-only), in the same order. |
| osv-scalibr `semantic/testdata/alpine-versions.txt` | A comment in the file says its cases are "from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alpinelinux/apk-tools/master/tests/version.data"; 729 of its 778 pairs are in that file. |
| osv-scalibr `semantic/testdata/redhat-versions.txt` | 96 of the 103 pairs in rpm's `tests/rpmvercmp.at` (GPL-2.0-or-later) appear in it. |

Before vendoring another file from these sources, check that it is not derived from a copyleft test
suite. The tool-generated osv-scalibr files (`*-generated.txt`) and `debian-versions.txt` (none of its
versions occur in dpkg's `t-version.c`) were checked and are fine to use.
